findings.title: Negative cursor offsets crash the request instead of enabling "advanced pagination"
findings.description:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset` when `enable_advanced_features` is set. Django (pinned at 5.2.1) raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` on negative queryset slices, so the comment "The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false.

The offset is caller-controlled: `Cursor.from_string` at `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:59` accepts any `int`, so `?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-5:0` reaches this branch. `paginate()` at `src/sentry/api/base.py:540` only catches `BadPaginationError`, so the result is an unhandled 500.

The inline comment says this "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", which is not a property an audit-log endpoint should have. Reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError`, as the other paginators in this file do (lines 287, 351, 701, 748, 804), and delete the branch.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate a datetime column
findings.description:
`get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value. Both are copied from the numeric `Paginator` (lines 222-227). The endpoint uses it with `order_by="-datetime"` at `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:76-83`.

- **Any non-empty page:** `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])`, and `math.ceil(datetime)` raises `TypeError`.
- **Any follow-up cursor:** `build_queryset` compares the timestamp column against a bare integer instead of a datetime.

The `optimized_pagination=true` path therefore returns a 500 for any organization with at least one audit log entry. `DateTimePaginator` (lines 230-241) has the correct conversions.

findings.title: `organization_context.member` is dereferenced without a None check on every request
findings.description:
`enable_advanced` is computed unconditionally, before the `use_optimized` check. `RpcUserOrganizationContext.member` is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None`, documented as None when the user has no membership (`src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346`).

Any caller that is not `is_superuser` and has no member row raises `AttributeError`. That includes token or API-key access that passes `OrganizationAuditPermission` without a membership. This regresses the default path too, not only the opt-in one.

findings.title: Gating uses the wrong privilege signals
findings.description:
Two problems with the "authorized administrators" gate:

- **`has_global_access` is not an admin signal.** It is a team-access flag on the member (`model.py:134`), not a role or scope check.
- **`request.user.is_superuser` bypasses the active-superuser convention.** The permission class for this endpoint uses `is_active_superuser(request)` (`src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124`).

The behaviour is also switched by an undocumented query parameter, `optimized_pagination`, rather than a feature flag or option.

findings.title: BasePaginator change affects every paginator and its comment is wrong
findings.description:
This line is shared by `Paginator`, `DateTimePaginator` and all other `BasePaginator` subclasses.

- **Forward cursors:** a negative offset is now silently clamped to 0. The other paginators in the file raise `BadPaginationError`.
- **`is_prev` cursors:** the negative offset is passed straight to the queryset slice and still raises `ValueError`, giving a 500.

The comment claims negative offsets are allowed and "safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions"; neither is true. The comment added at `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27` likewise describes a behaviour change that the code does not make.

findings.title: `get_result` is a near-verbatim copy of the base implementation
findings.description: About 65 lines of `BasePaginator.get_result` are duplicated, with the explanatory comments stripped. The only difference is the negative-offset branch, and its `else` arm is identical to the base class. The docstring's claims ("optimized query path", "streamlined boundary condition handling") match nothing in the code. If a distinct paginator is really needed, subclass `DateTimePaginator` and override only what differs.

findings.title: Span eviction limit is hard-coded in Lua and the Python limit is now dead
findings.description:
`zpopmin` drops the earliest-ending spans once a segment exceeds a literal 1000.

- **Dead parameter:** `max_segment_spans` (`src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:150,158`) is no longer read anywhere.
- **Lost observability:** the removed check in `_load_segment_data` emitted `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded` and an error log. Nothing replaces it, so spans are now dropped with no metric or log.

Pass the limit as an ARGV from `max_segment_spans` and return the evicted count so `process_spans` can emit a metric.

findings.title: SET to ZSET change reuses the same key namespace
findings.description: `span-buf:s:*` keys written by the previous version are Redis SETs. After this change, `ZADD`, `ZCARD`, `ZUNIONSTORE` and `ZSCAN` on those keys return `WRONGTYPE`. That fails the pipeline in `process_spans` and `_load_segment_data` for any segment in flight during a rollout, until `redis_ttl` (3600s) expires. A key-prefix bump or a drain step would avoid this. The module docstring (lines 38-39, 58) still describes the storage as sets.

findings.title: No tests for the new behaviour
`zunionstore` uses the default SUM aggregate
findings.description: If the same payload is present in both sets being merged, its score becomes the sum of the two end timestamps, which skews `zpopmin` ordering. `AGGREGATE MAX` would keep the score meaningful.

findings.title: Redirect loop bound cut from 10000 to 1000 with its comment removed
findings.description: The limit is ten times lower, and the comment explaining the consequence (deep segment trees may not be joined correctly) was deleted rather than updated. The change is unrelated to the eviction work and is unexplained.

findings.title: `cast(SpanEvent, ...)` does not validate the payload
findings.description: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises `KeyError` on a payload missing the field, and a `None` value would fail in `zadd`. This matches how `trace_id` and `span_id` are already accessed, so it is not a new pattern, but the cast gives type-checker comfort only.

findings.title: Formatting
findings.description: There is trailing whitespace at lines 72 and 89 here, and in the `OptimizedCursorPaginator` docstring (`src/sentry/api/paginator.py:824,827`). There are also three blank lines before the class at `paginator.py:818-820`. The project's black/flake8 hooks will reject these.

findings.title: ZSCAN result handling and fixture updates
findings.description: With redis-py 3.4.1, `zscan` returns `(cursor, [(member, score), ...])`. The unpacking in the size accounting and `payloads[key].extend(...)` is correct. Every `Span(...)` construction in `tests/sentry/spans/test_buffer.py` and `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py` supplies the new required field.
